id.description: Citation marker as it appears in the paper (e.g. '1', '12', 'Smith2020')

authors.description: Author names in 'Last, First' format (e.g. 'Vaswani, Ashish'). For single-name authors, use the name as-is.

relation.description: How this reference relates to the citing paper, judged from in-text citation context.

roles.description: Functional relation(s) this reference plays for the citing paper, drawn from the same vocabulary as the unit-graph edges; one or more. builds_on=a direct predecessor THIS paper's contribution builds on, improves, or extends (the cited method your work descends from); uses=a method/architecture/algorithm/technique/tool/optimizer/library/dataset/benchmark reused as a building block, not the contribution's lineage; compares_to=compared against experimentally (a baseline) or critiqued/disagreed with (the `stance` field carries supportive/neutral/critical); background=field/concept context, motivation, future-work mention, or passing related mention. builds_on/uses/compares_to each reconcile to the unit-graph edge of the same name; background is the only context-only role (no edge) and is mutually exclusive — emit it alone, never alongside a structural role. When ambiguous between builds_on and background, prefer builds_on if the cited work is plausibly a direct predecessor (high recall); use background only when no stronger role fits.

stance.description: How the citing paper positions itself: critical if the paper critiques or contrasts the work; supportive if it explicitly endorses or adopts the work's approach as its own foundation (or roles includes builds_on); otherwise neutral (plain usage of a resource, plain baseline). Default neutral.

salience.description: central = load-bearing for this paper's argument or experiments (a main baseline, a core building block, or relied on repeatedly); peripheral = passing mention.

provides_name.description: For builds_on, uses, and compares_to, the single most specific named artifact the citing paper takes from or compares against this work (e.g. 'Transformer', 'ImageNet', 'Adam', 'BERT'). Empty string for background or when no concrete artifact is named.

provides_unit_ids.description: Always output an empty array []. Links to spine unit IDs are filled deterministically by the pipeline after section extraction; never populate this yourself.
